subject: Solution validation: Aperture Analytics connector & telemetry plan
messages:
From: Emma James <emma.james@aperture.ai>
To: mina_haddad@redwoodai.com
Cc: ctf-support@aperture.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Aperture - Redwood connector feasibility

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this call last week. As discussed, Aperture Analytics is evaluating a native connector into Redwood Inference so we can route anonymized telemetry and inference metrics from our platform into customers' Redwood deployments (hosted + private). Attached is our initial integration spec (product_integration_spec_v1.pdf).

High-level asks from our side:
- Simple managed connector for hosted customers (API/webhook)
- Optional on-prem sidecar pattern for private deployments (TLS + mutual auth)
- Streaming of inference events (token-level timing + meta) and periodic batch archives for billing reconciliation

Can your team confirm whether Redwood supports the sidecar model (k8s daemonset or systemd service) and whether we can push protobuf/JSON over gRPC or must fall back to HTTP POST? Also need to understand maximum payload sizes and recommended backoff.

Emma
Integration Lead, Aperture Analytics

Attachment: product_integration_spec_v1.pdf (PDF, 256KB)
From: mina_haddad@redwoodai.com
To: Emma James <emma.james@aperture.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodai.com, sergio_alvarez@redwoodai.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 11:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aperture - Redwood connector feasibility

Emma — thanks for the spec, looks straightforward. Looping in Laura and Sergio to validate architecture and test coverage. Quick summary from our side and proposed next steps: 

Summary of fit:
- Hosted: we can accept HTTP POST or gRPC streaming into a dedicated ingestion endpoint; prefer gRPC for token-level streaming to preserve ordering.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): sidecar model works — we typically recommend a lightweight TLS-terminating sidecar run as a DaemonSet. Mutual TLS (mTLS) with cert rotation via customer KMS is supported.

Proposed validation plan (canary → pilot → GA):
1) Architecture review and compatibility checklist (this week) — owner: Laura
2) Implementation of a gRPC shim + HTTP fallback (Aperture devs + Redwood sample) — 2 weeks dev
3) Canary on a Redwood Dedicated pool with synthetic replay (3 days) — owner: Sergio
4) Pilot with 1 enterprise customer (opt-in) — 2–4 weeks

Questions for your engineers:
- Do you have protobuf schemas we should review, or will you provide JSON payloads?
- Any data residency constraints for pilot customers?
- Expected per-customer QPS and typical event batch size?

I've attached a simple architecture diagram and will draft a test matrix after Laura reviews. Proposed call to sync devs: Thu 2026-11-05 10:00 PT (Zoom link in follow-up).

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Partner Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwoodai.com

Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwoodai.com
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aperture - Redwood connector feasibility

Thanks — reviewed the spec and Mina's summary. A few technical notes and proposed test cases we should include in the matrix: 

Auth and handshake:
- Support API-key for hosted; OAuth2 authorization code flow is optional for marketplace users. For private, mTLS only.
- Cert rotation: integration needs to accept CA rotations signed by customer KMS within 48h window.

Transport & payloads:
- Prefer gRPC streaming for token-level telemetry. Fall back to HTTP POST for batch ingestion (max 5MB per POST).
- Protobuf preferred; we can accept JSON but conversion step will add 10–12ms per event on average.

Performance and resilience test cases:
- Throughput ramp: 0 -> expected peak (test at 2x)
- Latency tail p99 under streaming load
- Backpressure/backoff behavior when Redwood ingress is saturated
- Data loss tests during failover (simulate sidecar restart)

I'll attach a starter test-matrix and mark responsible owners. Sergio — can you own the canary execution and the load harness?

Laura Bennett
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Laura / Mina — great, thanks for the clarity and the matrix. Quick answers from Aperture engineering: 

- Protobuf first; we will publish .proto files by EOD Monday.
- Typical pilot QPS: 50–150 per customer, spikes to ~600 for large customers.
- Batch archives: we can do gzipped JSON (up to 50MB files) for reconciliation windows.
- Data residency: pilot customers are US-only; enterprise customers will require EU-only routing later.

We've opened a partner NDA internally — I will send a DocuSign link and the proto package. Also confirmed Thu 2026-11-05 10:00 PT still works for our eng lead; Zoom: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210

Emma
